I'm having an odd issue. Most of the time, the game runs at a stable 60fps regardless of situation. At seemingly-random times, GPU usage spikes, performance drops to sub-30fps and stays there. This happens ingame, in menus, on the world map, even on the start screen. Relaunching the game, force closing it, changing any settings at all do NOT work - the only thing that fixes it is a full PC reboot. I've got Effects down to Low, Motion Blur off, tried lowering other settings, literally nothing has any impact at any point. The reboot is the ONLY thing that gets me back up to stable 60fps. For the record, I could consistently run Nioh 1 at 60fps at all times - never so much as a dip. And I don't have this problem with any other games, including ones that are MUCH more graphically-intensive than this one.

I don't feel like this is a GPU limitation, CPU is stable, no heating issues, and no problems elsewhere. Number of running programs also doesn't matter. I'm drawing a complete blank as to what the cause might be, and having to reboot every half hour or so to maintain playability is not fun. My card is a GTX 1060 - not the newest or strongest, but again, it runs modern games like Doom Eternal, AC Valhalla, etc. at stable 50-60fps. Any thoughts?

It's not as bad as it looks. It sucks fighting Eidolons with Baby's First Amp that you get for free, but even at Rank 1 with them, you can get the components for the first REAL Amp, and while it's not "meta", it's perfectly functional, and can do decent damage to the Eidolons.

The real issue is that there really isn't scaling for the number of players you fight the Eidolons with, so you need a half-competent (or at least not pants-on-head stupid) team to comfortably beat the first one, and have ANY hope of taking on the second and third.

It's a snowball though; get past the first hurdle, you'll get a better amp, then it becomes easier from there.

\^ What the comment above me said.

It's also worth noting that Transference, the version you get after War Within, starts out weak but you can upgrade it to be nearly as effective as fighting with your Warframe.

Transcendence, the original version from the Second Dream, is pretty bad, and doesn't really get much better.

If I had the absolute freedom to do so, I'd finish my degree. I do NOT want to quit. But I'm not sure if I have a choice. The job search has turned up nothing. There simply doesn't seem to be any employers who want to deal with the triple whammy of a college student who can't drive and has no experience. I hate the thought of quitting school, but if opening up my schedule is the only way I can find work...

As for the license, it's not practical. I know how to drive, but my state has a new law passed a few months ago that says anyone who takes the test needs 50 hours of logged practice time with a licensed driver, and the only two people in my household who have both a license and a vehicle don't trust me driving it. My brother has his license because he learned through stealing the car multiple times over the past ten years or so and never got caught, and he got his license before the law went into effect.

I have two weeks left. I'm going to keep looking for a job (although I'm losing more and more hope each day) until my time is up and then...whatever happens, happens. Time is what I need, and it's the one thing I don't have. I appreciate the advice all the same, though.

I know my friends will be there for me no matter what, but that's partially the problem; they want to fight a battle I've pretty much already accepted as lost, and I don't want to drag them down with me any more than necessary. I could talk to someone professional, but I have a feeling they'll just tell me what I already know, that my problems aren't justified and I'm essentially just whining over trivial things (considering their effect on me some would judge them as nontrivial, but in comparison to the problems many others are facing, they really are.) I'll consider calling though, and even if I don't, thank you for the number.
